About a-frame signs

A-Frame Signs that hold up outdoors.

Sidewalk displays with interchangeable sign faces. Printed in-house on a latex large-format press with UV-stable inks, so colour stays true through a season of sun and rain.

Every large-format order includes finishing — hemming, grommets, stakes, frames or poles as the product needs — and a digital proof at scale so you can see how the layout reads from across a room or a parking lot.

UV-stable inks

Latex inks rated for 2–3 years outdoors unlaminated.

Finished, not just printed

Hems, grommets and hardware included where listed.

Custom sizes

Standard formats or any size up to 10 ft wide seamless.

Ready in days

Most pieces ship in 2–3 business days after proof.

Guidelines & file prep

Big prints, simple file rules.

Large format is forgiving on resolution but strict on file type and colour. Here’s what works.

Final size24 × 36 in faces
ScaleBuild at 100% or at 25% with 4× resolution
Resolution100–150 DPI at final size (300 DPI is unnecessary and huge)
Bleed1 in on all sides for banners; 0.25 in for rigid signs
ColourCMYK; Pantone references welcome for brand colours
File typesPDF, AI, EPS · TIFF or JPG at 150 DPI for photos
FontsOutlined — banners are often edited last-minute, so send editable too
  1. Start from the templateSet up your document at the final size with the bleed and safe area shown in the table.
  2. Work in CMYK at 300 DPIConvert RGB images before export; anything under 150 DPI at print size will look soft.
  3. Outline fonts, embed imagesOr send the fonts along. Linked images that aren’t embedded arrive as grey boxes.
  4. Export a print-ready PDFPDF/X-1a or “High Quality Print” with crop marks and bleed. Single pages, not spreads.
  5. We proof before we printYou’ll get a digital proof to approve. Nothing goes to press until you sign off.
Keep important text at least 3 in from banner edges where grommets and hems land.

Preguntas frecuentes

Questions we get asked most.

Still unsure? Send us a note and we’ll answer within one business day.

All FAQsContáctanos
How long will it last outside?
Vinyl banners and coroplast signs are rated for 2–3 years outdoors. Flags see more wind stress and typically last 6–12 months in constant use. Roll-ups and X-frames are indoor products.
Can you install it?
Yes — choose “Installation requested” and we’ll quote hanging, mounting or staking on site across the GTA.
Is the hardware included?
Where the configurator says so, yes: grommets on banners, H-stakes with yard signs, the stand with roll-ups, the pole kit with flags and the frame with A-frames. Replacement graphics alone are available for all of them.
What resolution do I need?
Far less than you’d think. 100–150 DPI at final size is plenty for a banner read from a metre or more away. A logo as vector will always be sharp at any size.
Can I order one, or is there a minimum?
No minimum. One banner, one sign, one flag — pricing scales down at quantity, but single pieces are welcome.
13 oz or 18 oz?
13 oz is the standard for most banners. 18 oz is heavier and stiffer — choose it for permanent outdoor installs or anything wider than 8 ft.

Need a-frame signs by a date?

Tell us the size, quantity and the day you need them. We’ll confirm production and installation slots straight away.
